objective: Sell and deliver two bounded USD 500 MCP boundary reviews using executed first-party proof, review-first intake, and agent-run fulfillment.

strategy.target_math: 2 paid reviews x USD 500 = USD 1,000 gross before fees, tax, refunds, and delivery costs
strategy.why_now: Current paid listings ask for real MCP servers, reproducible environments, deterministic verification, authentication and scoping controls, auditability, and failure handling. The owned LKT server supplies inspectable first-party proof for a smaller fixed offer.
strategy.operator_involvement: The agent can discover demand, qualify metadata, prepare scope, run the bounded review, assemble evidence, and record delivery. The operator is needed only when a customer requires an identity action, contract acceptance, unsupported expert judgment, or access that cannot be safely delegated.

demand_evidence.need: MCP Expert work covering real MCP tools, reproducible environments, deterministic verification, golden solutions, bugs, features, refactoring, and performance.
demand_evidence.boundary: This is a separate output-paid role with personal interview and assessment gates, not a buyer for this fixed service or evidence of revenue.

demand_evidence.need: A current worldwide listing asks for real MCP integrations with authentication, scoping, audit controls, least privilege, logs, and documentation.
demand_evidence.boundary: The listing requires unsupported conventional tenure and full-time overlap, so it is demand evidence only and was not applied to.

offer.delivery: Within seven business days after secured payment, repository access, working setup instructions, and every agreed test dependency are available. Only one MCP review is active at a time.
offer.scope: Map the reviewed MCP surface to real reads, writes, external calls, credentials, approval points, and failure impact; run ten agreed checks in one disposable environment; deliver a frozen inventory, sanitized protocol packet, failure ledger, and go/no-go report.
excluded: fix implementation or a second server, revision, transport, tool, resource, or test set
penetration testing, security certification, or a guarantee that the server is secure or production-ready
OAuth or authentication implementation, production deployment, SLA, performance guarantee, or ongoing monitoring
production secrets, private data, destructive live operations, or external writes unless separately authorized and scoped
offer.cancellation: Cancel before private access or execution begins for a full refund. Once work starts, refund only undelivered items using the fixed deliverable allocation.
offer.data_policy: Collect metadata only during the fit check. Agree repository access, fixtures, network behavior, credentials handling, confidentiality, retention, and permitted automation before work. Customer material never becomes public proof without separate written permission.
offer.payment_policy: After a positive fit check and accepted written scope, direct-site clients receive one reviewed Stripe request. Marketplace-origin contracts and payments stay on that marketplace. This is not a public self-serve checkout.

public_proof.subject: Local Knowledge Terminal MCP bridge
public_proof.decision: GO for the recorded local read-only scope; NO-GO for direct remote exposure because the standalone HTTP bridge has no client authentication.
public_proof.boundary: Project-owned evidence, not a customer result, penetration test, security certification, or promise of production fitness.

owned_delivery.homepage: The six-route chooser replaces the lower-priority Story Clip card with this current software-first offer in thirteen locales.
owned_delivery.verification: All 29 website contract tests passed. Desktop and mobile renders had no horizontal overflow. The offer, sample, fit check, archive, checksum, and tracked homepage route returned HTTP 200; the live archive was byte-identical to the committed packet.

intake.live_round_trip: On 2026-09-12, the live form made no endpoint request during local review, then one explicitly confirmed synthetic request was encrypted, accepted, authenticated, decrypted, validated, saved locally with mode 0600, and deleted unchanged from the remote spool. A second receiver pass returned no_pending. The exact local synthetic inquiry and envelope were removed after verification; sanitized receipt evidence was retained.

postiz.content:
An MCP server can be described as “read-only” and still expose private context through its outputs.

I tested that boundary in Local Knowledge Terminal with the official Python MCP SDK: two tools, one resource, 14 focused tests, and one frozen protocol packet. The result is deliberately narrow: GO for the recorded local read-only setup; NO-GO for direct remote exposure until client authentication is added.

The report and downloadable packet are here:
https://lazying.art/mcp-boundary-review/sample-report/?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=mcp_boundary_review&utm_content=executed_sample

The same method is now available as a fixed USD 500 review of one server, one revision, and ten agreed checks. Fit check first; no source upload or payment before scope.
